newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up on possible carryover buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up on possible carryover buying.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen gaining on Monday as buyers follow through on Friday's 3.33 percent gains following the appointment of Thanong Bidhya as finance minister, analysts said.
The SET Index gained 15.48 points to 480.25 on Friday as Thanong's appointment was cautiously welcomed the after the abrupt resignataion of his predecessor Amnuay Viravan.

"I think today we might see the market go up. At the beginning of the week people will be buying through, though later it is likely to drop off," said Pattera Dilokrungthirapop, head of research at SocGen Crosby Securities.
But worries ahead of a parliamentary budget debate on June 25 and a release of key central bank monthly economic data due on Thursday were likely to keep the market on edge, she said.
There were also renewed concerns surrounding the currency as the new finance minister's initiatives on the embattled baht were awaited, analysts said.

Possible announcement of revised corporate merger rules to help the on-going consolidation process among finance firms could also spark some speculative interest in the sector, analysts said. Local media said the government was planning decrees to bail out the crisis-ridden economy.
